bridges.statement: Religion provides justified orientation, meaning, and knowledge about realities that scientific measurement cannot exhaust.
Questions of value, purpose, and a good life cannot be settled by scientific description alone.
Human experience, consciousness, moral order, and the intelligibility of the world support belief in transcendent reality.
Lived and interpreted religious traditions can cultivate humility, community, moral development, and exemplary conduct.
Religious abuse is best addressed through healthier interpretation and practice rather than rejection of religion altogether.
Religion does not provide justified knowledge beyond evidence-based inquiry, even when it supplies meaning or consolation.
Human wellbeing, morality, and mental life concern objective conditions that evidence-based inquiry can increasingly investigate.
Religious convictions make claims about reality and should be proportioned to publicly assessable evidence.
Protected religious authority can preserve unsupported doctrines and motivate harms that depend upon those doctrines.
Open contemporary inquiry can preserve meaning and morality while correcting inherited claims without granting them special authority.
